## Problem

## Problem

Implement a routine that traverses a file-system tree and deletes every file that is marked as read-only. You are given an absolute path pointing to the entry point; all read-only files located anywhere beneath that path must be removed.

The path follows the hierarchical form `root/folder1/folder2/.../folderN/file.ext`.

## Example

Input: root/folder1/read_only_file.txt

Output:

(read_only_file.txt is a read-only file residing directly under folder1 — it is deleted, so no output is produced.)

## Constraints

- The path is guaranteed to be absolute.
- You must handle arbitrarily deep nesting of directories.
- Only files that have the read-only attribute set should be removed; all other files and all directories must remain untouched.
- You may assume the existence of a helper that provides file metadata (e.g., `is_read_only(path)` and `delete_file(path)`).

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Traverse the file system recursively using a stack or depth-first search.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

For each file, check its read-only attribute before attempting deletion.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Be cautious with permission errors and symbolic links that may cause loops.

</details>
